title.narrative: Enhancing Equitable Access to Life-Saving WASH Services for Drought-Affected and Hard-to-Reach Populations in Beledweyne, Hiraan

description.narrative: ltpgtIn 2025, Somalia remains entrenched in a protracted humanitarian crisis driven by prolonged drought, erratic rainfall, and recurrent flooding. These climate-induced shocks—exacerbated by conflict and widespread displacement—have severely disrupted access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services. Beledweyne district in the Hiraan region is among the most critically affected, where the failure of seasonal rains and flood-damaged infrastructure has left thousands of internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host communities reliant on unsafe water sources and exposed to escalating public health risks.ltbrgtRecent assessments estimate that over 5.24 million people across Somalia will require WASH assistance in 2025. In Beledweyne, deteriorating WASH conditions have led to increased cases of waterborne diseases, particularly among women, children, and marginalized groups. Communities lack access to clean water, effective treatment methods, and functional sanitation infrastructure, undermining health, dignity, and resilience.ltbrgtTo respond to these urgent needs, Dignity First Somalia (DFS) proposes an 8-month standalone WASH intervention reaching approximately 12,254 vulnerable people across Beledweyne and surrounding hard-to-reach villages. The project will deliver lifesaving and sustainable WASH activities that includeltbrgt Construction and rehabilitation of strategic water systems, with integrated chlorination to ensure safe water for drinking and household useltbrgt Installation of flood-resilient, gender-segregated, and disability-accessible latrines in both community settings and key institutions like health and nutrition centersltbrgt Distribution of hygiene kits and sanitation tools tailored to household needs and seasonal risksltbrgt Hygiene promotion campaigns focused on behavior change, water safety, and disease preventionltbrgt Continuous water quality monitoring to reduce contamination risks and protect public health.ltbrgtThe project is grounded in the Centrality of Protection Strategy (2025–2026) and integrates protection mainstreaming, gender equality, and disability inclusion throughout. Community engagement, inclusive WASH committees, and accessible feedback mechanisms will ensure that services are safe, responsive, and aligned with the needs of women, girls, persons with disabilities, and other at-risk groups. By addressing critical WASH gaps while promoting protection, sustainability, and local ownership, the project aims to improve public health, reduce displacement risks, and restore dignity for some of Somalia’s most vulnerable populations.ltbrgtlt/pgt
